A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WR-CP research. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material across the extensive appendix reorganization.

before.justification: Section 6 and the appendices report original six-dataset experiments, including coverage, prediction-set sizes, distance correlations, and ablations.

after.justification: The original empirical study is retained, with an expanded importance-weighting ablation reported in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The objective in Equation (19), Algorithm 1, importance weighting, and inference procedure are unchanged. The unweighted ablation variant already appeared in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use Airfoil, Seattle-loop, PeMSD4, PeMSD8, U.S.-States, and Japan-Prefectures with the same regression tasks and source-mixture scenarios. The synthetic illustrations are also retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain vanilla CP, IW-CP, CQR, and WC-CP, plus WR-CP(uw) and Hybrid WC-WR in supplementary analyses. The distance comparison retains TV, KL, and expectation difference.

E3.justification: Sampling procedures, model architecture, metrics, alpha values, and beta settings are retained. The weighting ablation's increased trial count changes replication, assessed under E5, without changing its evaluation design.

E4.justification: The weighting ablation in v1 Appendix D.3 becomes a revised ten-trial analysis in v2 Appendix C, still testing the same weighting component. Beta sensitivity, hybrid WC-CP, and coverage-guarantee analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The weighting ablation explicitly expands from the first sampling trial to all ten trials. The main experiments already used ten trials and reported variability; no new significance-testing or confidence-interval procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Headline coverage gap changes from 3.1% to 3.2%, and set-size reduction from 38% to 37%. In the expanded weighting ablation, WR-CP/WR-CP(uw) gaps change from 2.7%/2.2% to 3.1%/2.3%, and relative size reduction from 22.3% to 28.0%. These ablation summaries use different trial coverage, so they are not matched-setting performance gains. Main benchmark plots and tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–4, their proofs, assumptions, and appendix derivations are retained. Equation (2) adds denominator parentheses to match the 1/(n+1) bound already stated in v1's adjacent prose; this repairs a display typo without changing the underlying theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction slightly weaken the quantitative headline benefits from 3.1% coverage gap and 38% smaller sets to 3.2% and 37%. The claimed methodological contributions, applicability, and controllable trade-off remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The revised ablation discussion interprets typically smaller size variability as reduced adaptiveness, replacing v1's argument from zero variability to absent adaptiveness. The other mechanism explanations and limitations concerning KDE and calibration distributions are retained.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 newly states that code is released and supplies a repository URL. Existing architecture, sampling, density-estimation, and hyperparameter documentation is retained; repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: V2 adds Einbinder et al. (2022b), Training uncertainty-aware classifiers with conformalized deep learning, and refines discussion of training-based CP and prior worst-case approaches. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The appendices are substantially reorganized: the TV comparison, weighting rationale, and geometric explanation become dedicated Appendices B–D; estimation and experiments move to E–F; coverage analyses move to G with reversed subsection order; limitations become H. Main-text edits add navigation, author contacts, and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: All twenty figures and both tables are retained. Appendix figures are relocated and repacked beside their explanations, illustrations receive limited graphical edits, and the weighting-ablation plot is updated. Figure 4's caption corrects IW-CP to WR-CP. Most plot structures and the overall visual format remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Expanding the weighting ablation from one to ten trials provides more representative supporting evidence. Added code-access information and clearer appendix organization improve usability and reproducibility documentation. These are limited gains: the core method, theoretical development, and most experimental evidence remain unchanged.
